message:
## Vulnerability Digest

The 24-hour window was **2026-08-31 05:10 IST to 2026-09-01 05:10 IST** (2026-08-30 23:40 UTC to 2026-08-31 23:40 UTC). This primary scan read, normalized, combined, and deduplicated only `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt`; `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

Fresh, credible notices were verified for monitored Ubuntu, MySQL, OpenJDK, and OpenSSL scope. Canonical did not state severity ratings in the notices below, so severity is reported as **not clearly stated** rather than inferred.

**Finding 1: MySQL security update (USN-8700-1)**
- Product: MySQL on Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS
- Issue: 29 CVEs listed by Canonical, including CVE-2026-46936, CVE-2026-60183, and CVE-2026-60585
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notice
- Why it matters: Canonical published updated MySQL 8.0/8.4 packages for multiple security issues; both MySQL and Ubuntu are monitored products.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8700-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8700-1)

**Finding 2: OpenJDK security update (USN-8689-1 and related CRaC JDK notices)**
- Product: OpenJDK 26 and CRaC JDK 17/21/25 on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- Issue: Nine deduplicated CVEs: CVE-2026-46917, CVE-2026-46968, CVE-2026-47010, CVE-2026-47021, CVE-2026-47027, CVE-2026-47059, CVE-2026-47063, CVE-2026-60147, and CVE-2026-41254
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notices
- Why it matters: Authentication and authorization errors in JSSE, ImageIO, Security, Libraries, and 2D components could permit sensitive-data access or modification and denial of service. OpenJDK and Ubuntu are directly monitored.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8689-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8689-1)

**Finding 3: OpenSSL incomplete-fix correction (USN-8678-3)**
- Product: OpenSSL on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- Issue: CVE-2026-75803
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notice
- Why it matters: Canonical reported that its earlier update omitted the fix for an AEAD authentication-tag verification flaw that could permit forgery; the new notice corrects that omission. OpenSSL and Ubuntu are directly monitored.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8678-3](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8678-3)

**Finding 4: WebKitGTK security update (USN-8703-1)**
- Product: Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 LTS WebKitGTK packages
- Issue: 47 CVEs listed by Canonical
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notice
- Why it matters: A malicious website could trigger cross-site scripting, denial of service, or arbitrary code execution in applications using the affected web engine. Ubuntu is directly monitored.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8703-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8703-1)

**Finding 5: libssh security update (USN-8699-1)**
- Product: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS libssh packages
- Issue: CVE-2026-15370 and CVE-2026-59843 through CVE-2026-59850
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notice
- Why it matters: The flaws include SFTP/SSH denial of service, traffic integrity failure, information exposure, and memory-safety bugs with possible arbitrary code execution. This is relevant through the monitored Ubuntu platform; libssh is distinct from the separately monitored OpenSSH product.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8699-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8699-1)

**Finding 6: util-linux security update (USN-8702-1)**
- Product: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS util-linux packages
- Issue: CVE-2026-13595, CVE-2026-27456, CVE-2026-3184, and CVE-2026-53612 through CVE-2026-53615
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notice
- Why it matters: The flaws can cause information exposure, denial of service, host-access-control bypass, or local privilege escalation. Ubuntu is directly monitored.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8702-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8702-1)

**Finding 7: UDisks local privilege escalation (USN-8701-1)**
- Product: Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 LTS UDisks
- Issue: CVE-2026-7867
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notice
- Why it matters: A local console user could mount filesystems on behalf of privileged accounts, leading to privilege escalation. Ubuntu is directly monitored.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8701-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8701-1)

**Finding 8: OpenZFS authorization bypass (USN-8705-1)**
- Product: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS OpenZFS
- Issue: CVE-2026-79619
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notice
- Why it matters: A local attacker could bypass ioctl authorization checks to perform pool-administration operations or access privileged information. Ubuntu is directly monitored.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8705-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8705-1)

**Finding 9: FreeRDP security update (USN-8698-1)**
- Product: Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 LTS FreeRDP
- Issue: Multiple security issues; the notice does not list CVE identifiers
- Severity: Not clearly stated
- Why it matters: Canonical says the issues may expose information, crash FreeRDP, or permit arbitrary code execution. Ubuntu is directly monitored.
- Source: [Canonical USN-8698-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8698-1)

**Finding 10: Additional Ubuntu package advisories**
- Product: Ubuntu packages for GNU cpio, GNU Core Utilities, BIND, GNU diffutils, and attr
- Issues: CVE-2026-66484 through CVE-2026-66486; CVE-2025-5278 and CVE-2026-56391; CVE-2026-13204; CVE-2026-53910; CVE-2026-54371
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Canonical notices
- Why it matters: Canonical reports archive path/output manipulation, information exposure and crashes, remotely triggered BIND denial of service, diff3 denial of service, and attr local privilege escalation across supported Ubuntu releases.
- Sources: [cpio](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8704-1), [Core Utilities](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8697-1), [BIND](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8696-1), [diffutils](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8692-1), [attr](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8691-1)

**MongoDB ecosystem sweep**

MongoDB Server (Community and Enterprise), `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, major officially maintained libraries and services, MongoDB-owned advisories, NVD/CVE records, GitHub advisories, and CISA sources were checked.

No credible in-window MongoDB vulnerability was verified. An August 31 MongoDB C Driver release was found, but no authoritative source identified it as a security release, so it was not reported as a vulnerability.

**Possible matches needing review**

**PyCharm / JetBrains Cadence**
- Issue: CVE-2026-63077, Critical according to JetBrains
- Why it may match: JetBrains updated its Cadence incident notice on August 31. Cadence is an optional service/plugin integrated with monitored PyCharm, and JetBrains confirmed its TeamCity vulnerability was exploited against Cadence. Relevance depends on whether Cadence was used.
- Source: [JetBrains Cadence incident notice](https://blog.jetbrains.com/pycharm/2026/08/cadence-security-incident-august-2026/)

**WordPress / Kubio AI Website Builder plugin**
- Issue: CVE-2026-83492, Medium
- Why it may match: Tenable published a denial-of-service advisory on August 31 for a WordPress plugin. WordPress is monitored, but the plugin is not named in the inventory, so this matters only if Kubio AI Website Builder is installed.
- Source: [Tenable Research Advisories](https://www.tenable.com/security/research)

**Closing**

Immediate review is recommended for affected Ubuntu 26.04 systems because of the corrected OpenSSL fix and for deployments using the affected WebKitGTK, libssh, FreeRDP, UDisks, OpenZFS, util-linux, MySQL, or OpenJDK packages. Also confirm whether JetBrains Cadence or the Kubio WordPress plugin is deployed before treating either possible match as applicable.
